channel.title: Katali Journal
channel.description: Essays on craft, code & the spaces between

item.title: The Quiet Discipline of a Personal Website
item.description: A personal site is not a portfolio. It is a practice — a way of thinking in public, slowly, on the internet that only rewards speed.

item.title: What Moving to Nairobi Taught Me About Latency
item.description: Two hundred milliseconds changes how you design. A year of building and browsing from East Africa is a masterclass in the real cost of the prettiest code you can write.

item.title: Designing for Slow Connections
item.description: Performance is a design material. When latency is scarce, layout, typography, and motion all fall into line behind one question: what should the user see first?

item.title: Why I Write My Own CSS Instead of a Framework
item.description: Black velvet notebooks, seventy-five CSS variables, and a stubborn belief that one person's utility layer can be another person's actual design system.

item.title: The Case for Boring Technology
item.description: New tools are exciting. Old tools ship. A defense of the unglamorous stack that quietly meets its deadline, every time, for years.

item.title: On Finding Your Voice in Public
item.description: Impostor syndrome and the internet are a matched pair. A personal essay about writing more loudly, more often, and more kindly.

item.title: Field Notes: A Weekend in Lake Naivasha
item.description: Flat-calm water, papyrus birds, and the particular stillness of a place where the network drops out and nobody panics.

item.title: The Tyranny of the Infinite Feed
item.description: Endless scroll is not a feature, it is an architecture of avoidance. Why I installed brakes on the internet and started reading like it was 2010.

item.title: Notes on Building a Personal Knowledge System
item.description: No fancy tools. Just a folder, a naming convention, and the discipline of writing your future self a mail you will actually read.

item.title: Accessibility Is a Performance Budget
item.description: Screen readers and slow phones are the same sentence. A practical case for treating a11y like the performance constraint it always was.

item.title: Slow Food, Fast Code: Lessons from the Kitchen
item.description: Sous vide as a deployment strategy. Mise en place as a refactor. What a weekend of cooking taught me about running services people depend on.

item.title: Shipping Small: A Manifesto for Indie Builders
item.description: The roadmaps are the trap. The tiny, boring, finished product is the moat. Why small might be the only sustainable strategy left.
